SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

performance noun

a show, the performing of a play or music

also show, stage show, put on a play, the play is on, first night

classical

Cic. Mur. 72: spectācula sunt tribūtim data
Liv. 2.36.1: nōndum commissō spectāculō

spectāculum, spectāculī n.

noun, second declension

a show, a public performance

Any show put on for an audience, in the theatre or the circus; spectāculum committere, to begin the show (Livy). A concert is concentus (see concert).

Examples

  • haec cum data nova est, novum intervēnit vitium et calamitās, ut neque spectārī neque cognōscī potuerit

    when this play was first put on, a new mishap and disaster intervened, so that it could neither be watched nor followedTer. Hec. 1–3

  • ut pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs teneantur ob eamque rem vel famem et sitim perferant

    (we see children) held by a procession, games and shows of that kind, and putting up even with hunger and thirst for their sakeCic. Fin. 5.48

Other words

  • fābulam agere — put on, perform a play

    phrase: agō with fābulam; passive, fābula agitur, the play is on · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 33: cum prīmum eam agere coepī; Plaut. Men. 72: dum haec agitur fābula (Lewis & Short)

    A play is data when it is first put on (Ter. Hec. 1–2) and agitur while it is being performed.

See also play, concert, theatre, actor.
